title: Compare and Order Decimals

events.text: Does the decimal with more digits always have a greater value?
events.spoken_punctuation: Does the decimal with more digits always have a greater value?

events.text: Today we are comparing and ordering decimals.
events.spoken_punctuation: Today we are comparing and ordering decimals.

events.text: We will line up equal places, use placeholder zeros, and find the first place where the values differ.
events.spoken_punctuation: We will line up equal places, use placeholder zeros, and find the first place where the values differ.

events.text: Which would you predict is larger: four point six eight or four point six zero seven?
events.spoken_punctuation: Which would you predict is larger: four point six eight or four point six zero seven?

events.text: Our learning goal is to compare, order and locate decimal numbers using place value and number lines.
events.spoken_punctuation: Our learning goal is to compare, order and locate decimal numbers using place value and number lines.

events.text: Success criteria.
events.spoken_punctuation: Success criteria.

events.text: I can compare decimal digits from left to right.
events.spoken_punctuation: I can compare decimal digits from left to right.

events.text: I can use placeholder zeros to compare equivalent decimal forms.
events.spoken_punctuation: I can use placeholder zeros to compare equivalent decimal forms.

events.text: I can locate decimals accurately between labelled points on a number line.
events.spoken_punctuation: I can locate decimals accurately between labelled points on a number line.

events.text: Compare from left to right.
events.spoken_punctuation: Compare from left to right.

events.text: If the whole numbers match, compare tenths, then hundredths, then thousandths.
events.spoken_punctuation: If the whole numbers match, compare tenths, then hundredths, then thousandths.

events.text: Trailing zeros can show equal places without changing a value.
events.spoken_punctuation: Trailing zeros can show equal places without changing a value.

events.text: Decimal digits are not a separate whole number.
events.spoken_punctuation: Decimal digits are not a separate whole number.

events.text: Compare four point six eight and four point six zero seven.
events.spoken_punctuation: Compare four point six eight and four point six zero seven.

events.text: Rename four point six eight as four point six eight zero.
events.spoken_punctuation: Rename four point six eight as four point six eight zero.

events.text: The ones and tenths match.
events.spoken_punctuation: The ones and tenths match!

events.text: At the hundredths place, eight is greater than zero.
events.spoken_punctuation: At the hundredths place, eight is greater than zero.

events.text: That decides the comparison: four point six eight is greater.
events.spoken_punctuation: That decides the comparison: four point six eight is greater.

events.text: The thousandths cannot reverse it.
events.spoken_punctuation: The thousandths cannot reverse it.

events.text: Now compare zero point six two with zero point five nine nine.
events.spoken_punctuation: Now compare zero point six two with zero point five nine nine.

events.text: Both have zero whole ones.
events.spoken_punctuation: Both have zero whole ones.

events.text: At the tenths place, six is greater than five.
events.spoken_punctuation: At the tenths place, six is greater than five.

events.text: So zero point six two is greater, even though it has fewer written decimal digits.
events.spoken_punctuation: So zero point six two is greater, even though it has fewer written decimal digits.

events.text: Comparing sixty-two with five hundred and ninety-nine would compare the wrong units.
events.spoken_punctuation: Comparing sixty-two with five hundred and ninety-nine would compare the wrong units.

events.text: Which is greater: two point four zero five, or two point four five?
events.spoken_punctuation: Which is greater: two point four zero five, or two point four five?

events.text: Two point four five equals two point four five zero.
events.spoken_punctuation: Two point four five equals two point four five zero.

events.text: The first differing place is the hundredths, so two point four five is greater.
events.spoken_punctuation: The first differing place is the hundredths, so two point four five is greater!

events.text: Align equal place values and compare from the largest place.
events.spoken_punctuation: Align equal place values and compare from the largest place.

events.text: Stop at the first difference.
events.spoken_punctuation: Stop at the first difference.

events.text: On a number line the greater number is further right; the number of written digits alone does not decide.
events.spoken_punctuation: On a number line the greater number is further right; the number of written digits alone does not decide!
